newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SOCCER-BULGARIA'S HEAD COACH SAYS HE MAY RESIGN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BULGARIA'S HEAD COACH SAYS HE MAY RESIGN.

text.p: Bulgaria's head soccer coach Hristo Bonev said he would resign if Friday's extraordinary congress of the Bulgarian Football Union elected a new president he could not work with.
The football union's meeting follows accusations by some clubs of mismanagement and complaints by players.
"I told the players first...that if someone I cannot work with is elected, I will resign," Bonev, who has been coach for five months, said in a television interview on Tuesday.
Several players, including Lyuboslav Penev and striker Hristo Stoichkov, have demanded changes in the union's management.
Penev, dropped from the team for using insulting words on local television after the European championship in England, boycotted last Saturday's World Cup qualifier against Cyprus.
Stoichkov has vowed to quit the team unless the soccer chiefs are replaced.

Bonev, who said new blood was needed in the team, said the current president of the union Ivan Slavkov and the executive committee members had confidence in him and he would continue to work with them if they wanted him.
